intended_object: A Boolean test of whether a closed rational interval [lo, hi] is strictly positive, meaning every point of it is > 0. Inferred from the docstring and the name, in the context of an interval-arithmetic optimization engine.
explanation: `IntervalRat` is the library's structure for a closed interval: it has rational fields `lo` and `hi` and a proof `le : lo ≤ hi`, so it is never empty. Every point of [lo, hi] is strictly positive exactly when lo > 0. That is precisely what `I.lo > 0` tests, returned as a `Bool` (comparison on ℚ is decidable). Nothing goes wrong in degenerate cases: for a single point [a, a], the test gives a > 0, which is correct. Rational endpoints are a deliberate design choice of the library's computable interval arithmetic, and the check itself is trivial, so there is no broader Mathlib construction it should have reused. I found no Mathlib definition of this check: there is no Boolean positivity test on intervals of this kind. The definition is therefore faithful.
